newsitem.title: THAILAND: Bank of Thailand seeks to merge finance firms - paper.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Thailand seeks to merge finance firms - paper.

text.p: The Bank of Thailand on Monday will request powers to order immediate mergers among 33 troubled finance companies, the Nation newspaper said on Sunday.
The central bank will seek a decree from the cabinet giving it absolute authority to tackle the ailing financial sector, unnamed officials were quoted as saying.
The bank's move comes after earlier merger incentives failed, the report said.
The decree, if approved, would empower the central bank to order finance companies to merge without having to seek shareholder approval, the paper said.
Bank of Thailand Assistant Governor Siri Ganjarerndee confirmed authorities were looking at new measures, but denied the bank would seek a decree on Monday, the Bangkok Post newspaper said.
Thailand's finance and securities firms have been hit by declining asset quality brought about by troubled lending to an oversupplied property market and on consumer financing.
A much-vaunted plan to merge leading finance firm Finance One Plc, formally the country's leading finance firm, and medium-sized Thai Danu Bank Plc collapsed last month.

There are approximately 90 firms in the sector that have combined lending of around $58 billion. The exact extent of the problem loans is unknown but many analysts have estimated that about 10 percent are non-performing.
The firms have also seen the value of their securities portfolios decline on the battered local stock market, which closed on Friday at 566.39, less than half its value a year ago.
